title: NDCG@k
description:
Compute **normalised discounted cumulative gain at k**.

`ranked` lists the true relevance grades of the items in the order your ranker returned them. `ideal` is the list of relevance grades of **all** candidate items (in any order); the ideal ranking sorts them in descending order. Using the linear gain `gain = rel` and the discount `1 / log2(i + 2)` for the item at 0-based position `i`:

`DCG@k = sum_{i < k} ranked[i] / log2(i + 2)`

`IDCG@k` is the same sum over the sorted `ideal` list, and `NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k`. Only the first `k` positions of each list count (fewer if a list is shorter). Return `0.0` when `IDCG@k` is 0.

examples.explanation: Only the first three positions count: DCG = 3 + 1.2619 + 1.5, IDCG = 3 + 1.8928 + 1.
The only relevant item is at position 2, outside the cut-off.

hints: Write a helper dcg(rels, k) that sums rels[i] / log2(i + 2) over the first k entries; log2(i + 2) is 1 at position 0 so the top item is undiscounted.
IDCG uses sorted(ideal, reverse=True), truncated to k. Check for IDCG == 0 before dividing.
signature: def ndcgAtK(self, ranked: List[float], ideal: List[float], k: int) -> float:
approach:
**DCG rewards relevance placed early; dividing by the best achievable DCG makes queries comparable.** The logarithmic discount `1 / log2(position + 2)` drops slowly, encoding the assumption that users scan down a list with gradually decreasing attention. Normalising by IDCG (the DCG of the perfectly sorted list) maps every query into `[0, 1]`, so the metric can be averaged over queries with different numbers of relevant items.

Watch the off-by-one: with 0-based positions the discount is `log2(i + 2)` so the first item has discount 1. Truncate both lists to k before summing, and handle a query with no relevant items (IDCG 0) explicitly; conventions vary between returning 0 and skipping the query, so state yours.

**Interview follow-ups:** Why do many systems use the exponential gain `2^rel - 1` instead of linear gain? (it emphasises highly relevant items). How does NDCG compare with MAP or MRR, and which suits graded versus binary relevance? How would you optimise a model for NDCG when it is non-differentiable? (LambdaRank/LambdaMART, listwise losses). How does the metric behave when `ideal` contains relevant items the ranker never retrieved?

complexity.time: O(n log n) for sorting the ideal list
